heroImage.caption: FIRST UNITED redevelopment context — Source: FIRST UNITED

sections.label: Overview
sections.content:
FIRST UNITED is a longstanding Downtown Eastside organization focused on harm reduction, belonging, and systems change.

Its work integrates shelter, food, legal advocacy, and policy reform through community-centred service delivery.

The organization also leads redevelopment planning to expand community-serving space and secure long-term affordability outcomes.

Verified figures are listed in Quick Facts, with linked sources for each value.

highlights.title: Essential Services
highlights.description: Shelter, meals, and frontline support are delivered through low-barrier, harm-reduction practice.

highlights.title: Community Connection
highlights.description: Drop-in spaces, cultural care, and peer supports build safety and belonging.

highlights.title: Systems Change
highlights.description: Legal advocacy and research partnerships inform tenant protection and housing policy reform.

highlights.title: Redevelopment Program
highlights.description: A major site renewal process is underway to expand community infrastructure and below-market housing.

sections.label: Deeper Dive
sections.content:
Redevelopment Vision

FIRST UNITED is advancing a purpose-built facility designed around community priorities, accessibility, and cultural safety.

Integrated Service Model

Programs connect immediate supports with long-term stability through legal, social, and policy-focused work.

Research Partnership

Collaboration with housing researchers helps translate tenant experience into public policy and legal advocacy.
keyPoints: Community-led service delivery is core to the organization model
Harm reduction principles guide frontline programs
Legal advocacy and policy work are deeply integrated
Redevelopment planning focuses on long-term community benefit
Verified numeric values are provided in Quick Facts

sections.label: Overview
sections.content:
The Aboriginal Front Door Society is an Indigenous-led community hub in the Downtown Eastside.

Programs focus on cultural reconnection, daily support, and safe referrals grounded in Indigenous teachings.

The organization provides practical services while strengthening identity, kinship, and community resilience.

Verified figures are listed in Quick Facts, with linked sources for each value.

highlights.title: Cultural Programming
highlights.description: Talking circles, craft practices, and shared activities support cultural continuity and healing.

highlights.title: Drop-In Support
highlights.description: The site serves as a safe entry point for connection, language, and community services.

highlights.title: Storage and Safety
highlights.description: Practical supports include storage, referrals, and relationship-based outreach.

highlights.title: Food Programs
highlights.description: Food distribution and daily gathering space help stabilize community members facing insecurity.

sections.label: Programs & Role
sections.content:
Cultural Reconnection

The society advances Indigenous-led healing and wellness approaches rooted in tradition and lived experience.

Daily Supports

Programming combines practical care with culturally grounded community-building in a consistent drop-in environment.
keyPoints: Indigenous leadership anchors governance and program direction
Cultural practice is integrated into daily service delivery
Drop-in supports strengthen safety and belonging
Community referrals are grounded in trust and continuity

sections.label: Overview
sections.content:
The UBC Learning Exchange connects university resources with Downtown Eastside community priorities through reciprocal learning.

Programs focus on digital access, communication, and resident-informed education in a locally embedded setting.

The space also hosts community-engaged research that bridges academic analysis and lived expertise.

Verified figures are listed in Quick Facts, with linked sources for each value.

highlights.title: Resident-Informed Learning
highlights.description: Programs are designed with residents and partners rather than delivered as one-way outreach.

highlights.title: Digital and Communication Support
highlights.description: Workshops and practical coaching improve access to services, information, and participation.

highlights.title: Community Research Hosting
highlights.description: The site convenes dialogue between legal advocates, service providers, and community members.

highlights.title: Neighbourhood Integration
highlights.description: Local partnerships help align university activity with frontline priorities in the area.

sections.label: Programs
sections.content:
Program Model

The Learning Exchange builds programming through shared design with residents and community organizations.

Education and Inclusion

Core offerings support digital literacy, communication, and confidence-building for community participation.

Research and Civic Dialogue

Events and collaborations support policy discussion informed by both academic and lived knowledge.
keyPoints: Reciprocal learning is the foundation of program delivery
Resident priorities shape educational offerings
Community-engaged research is hosted on site
Partnerships connect campus and neighbourhood systems

sections.label: Overview
sections.content:
The Downtown Eastside Community Land Trust advances community ownership as an anti-displacement housing strategy.

Its governance model centres Indigenous leadership, tenant voice, and lived experience in major decisions.

Acquisition and operations work focuses on preserving affordability and strengthening resident control over housing outcomes.

Verified figures are listed in Quick Facts, with linked sources for each value.

highlights.title: Community Ownership Pathway
highlights.description: Building acquisitions are structured to secure long-term affordability and community control.

highlights.title: Operating Partnerships
highlights.description: Partnerships with public agencies support stabilization, renovations, and tenant protections.

highlights.title: Tenant and Elder Input
highlights.description: Decision-making includes ongoing input from tenants, elders, and resident leaders.

highlights.title: Child and Family Supports
highlights.description: Housing planning is linked with community-serving amenities and care infrastructure.

sections.label: Partners & Work
sections.content:
Acquisition Strategy

The trust focuses on securing vulnerable rental buildings and keeping them in community-serving ownership.

Governance Approach

Indigenous leadership and lived-experience participation guide priorities for operations, repairs, and tenant stability.

Public Partnership Role

Collaboration with public funders and service providers helps maintain affordability and improve building conditions.
keyPoints: Community ownership is used as a displacement prevention tool
Governance centres Indigenous and tenant leadership
Acquisitions are tied to long-term affordability outcomes
Operations emphasize resident stability and safety

sections.label: Overview
sections.content:
The DTES SRO Collaborative is a tenant-led network focused on safety, rights, and living conditions in private SRO housing.

Its programs combine harm reduction, tenant organizing, peer leadership, and building-level problem solving.

The collaborative also produces policy evidence through surveys and research partnerships that inform public action.

Verified figures are listed in Quick Facts, with linked sources for each value.

highlights.title: Tenant Committees
highlights.description: Resident committees identify priority issues and organize practical building improvements.

highlights.title: Peer Harm Reduction
highlights.description: Peer leaders deliver overdose response support and safer use resources in the places people live.

highlights.title: City Survey Partnership
highlights.description: Collaborative survey work strengthens visibility of tenant experience in policy planning.

highlights.title: Public Accountability
highlights.description: Research and advocacy continue to shape vacancy control and investment discussions.

sections.label: Programs
sections.content:
Tenant-Based Initiatives

Programs emphasize tenant leadership through committees, peer safety roles, and resident training pathways.

Survey and Research Work

Collaborative data collection documents living conditions and strengthens evidence for housing policy reform.

Advocacy and Systems Change

The network links frontline tenant organizing with legal and policy advocacy for stronger renter protections.
keyPoints: Tenant leadership drives program design and implementation
Peer-based safety work is central to the operating model
Survey evidence informs intergovernmental policy discussions
Advocacy targets stronger rights and living conditions

sections.label: Overview
sections.content:
Hogan's Alley Society leads cultural redress and community-owned development rooted in Black history in Vancouver.

Its work links housing, cultural infrastructure, and anti-displacement planning through a community land trust framework.

The society combines development planning with active programming, partnerships, and governance work grounded in community accountability.

Verified figures are listed in Quick Facts, with linked sources for each value.

highlights.title: Main Street Development Block
highlights.description: A major redevelopment block anchors long-term planning for housing, culture, and community-serving uses.

highlights.title: Cultural Centre Program
highlights.description: Planned cultural facilities are designed to support gathering, learning, art, and intergenerational community life.

highlights.title: Community Housing Operations
highlights.description: Current housing operations provide culturally grounded support for residents facing housing precarity.

highlights.title: Afrocentric Governance
highlights.description: Governance development emphasizes collective care, community accountability, and long-term stewardship.

sections.label: History & Plans
sections.content:
Historical Context and Redress

The society responds to historic displacement by rebuilding cultural, social, and economic infrastructure under community leadership.

Land Trust and Development Strategy

Planning work integrates affordable housing, cultural space, childcare, and local enterprise in a single community-owned framework.

Network and Partnership Work

Regional and national partnerships connect local implementation with broader land trust practice and policy learning.
keyPoints: Cultural redress and housing delivery are pursued together
Community ownership is central to long-term stewardship
Planning integrates housing, culture, care, and enterprise
Governance development is rooted in community accountability
Verified numeric values are provided in Quick Facts
